text: 64 clubs in a knockout cup. Pairings are drawn and the club drawn first has the home right; in a tie between a licensed-league club and an amateur club the amateur club is at home. A tie still level after extra time is decided on penalties. The final is played at the Olympiastadion in Berlin, which has hosted it since 1985; the State of Berlin reports an agreement that keeps it there until at least 2030. The length of extra time in the men's cup was not found.

text: Entrants: the Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs of the previous season (36), the champion and the next three clubs of the previous 3. Liga season (4), and the 21 winners of the regional association cups (Landespokal). The last three places go to the associations with the most teams, at most one extra each, decided by the DFB's Spielausschuss from membership statistics. Second teams of licensed clubs may not enter. If a Landespokal winner is not eligible or already qualified, the next-placed eligible team of that cup takes the place; if a 3. Liga club that qualified through the league wins its Landespokal, the loser of that final moves up. A second source counts the regional places differently (22 cup winners plus named extra places); the difference was not resolved.

text: Identity. The DFB's regulations call it the DFB-Vereinspokal (Herren); its own pages call it the DFB-Pokal der Männer. A men's competition at national (DFB) level, organised by the DFB; the regulations make the DFB GmbH & Co. KG the organiser of the final, which rents the stadium and fixes the venue. The 21 regional associations' cups (Verbandspokal) feed into it.
basis: published: Spielordnung § 45 Nr. 1.3 and § 46 Nr. 2.1, Durchführungsbestimmungen § 52

text: Entry rules: 64 teams. The Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs of the season just ended, the cup winners of the 21 regional associations, and the champion and the next three of the 3. Liga of the season just ended. The remaining places up to 64 go to the associations with the most men's teams, at most one extra each, decided by the DFB's Fachgruppe Spielbetriebe from the current membership statistics; every association must send at least one amateur team. Second teams of licensed clubs may not enter (since 2008-09), no club may enter two teams (since 2009-10), and the club's status in the season being played counts. A regional cup winner that is a second team or already qualified is replaced by the next eligible team of that cup; a 3. Liga qualifier that is a second team or already qualified through its regional cup is replaced by the next eligible 3. Liga team or the next eligible team of that cup. Merged teams (Spielgemeinschaften) may not enter. Each entrant must declare an advertising-free stadium for a live TV match, which need not be in its own town.
basis: published: Spielordnung § 45 Nr. 1.3

text: 2026-27 field: 64 teams, 32 first-round ties (30 in August 2026, two in early September 2026 for the two Supercup clubs). The DFB counts 13 clubs that play in the 3. Liga in 2026-27 in the first-round draw, a record; only four 3. Liga places come through the league, the others came through the regional cups. In the first round all 13 were at home against a Bundesliga or 2. Bundesliga club.
basis: published: DFB news of June 2026 and the 2026/2027 information page

text: Draw and home right. Rounds 1 and 2: two pots, one with the Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs and one with the amateur teams, by status in the season being played; in round 1 the clubs promoted to the 2. Bundesliga and the previous season's 15th of the 2. Bundesliga (and its 16th if it stayed up through the play-off) go in the amateur pot. A ball is drawn from the amateur pot first, then from the other; when one pot is empty the rest are drawn against each other; the team drawn first is always at home. Round of 16, quarter- and semi-finals: one pot, the team drawn first is at home, but between a licensed team and an amateur team the amateur team is at home. Home right cannot be given up; two teams that named the same stadium and are drawn together is not a waiver. Final at the venue the DFB GmbH & Co. KG fixes. Level after normal time: extra time of 2 x 15 minutes, then penalties. Five rounds and a final. No seeding and no neutral ground other than the final is stated.
basis: published: Spielordnung § 46 Nr. 2.1, Durchführungsbestimmungen § 49

text: Each tie is one match, with no second leg.

text: Draws and kick-off times. The first-round draw is set some weeks after the final, once the regional cups are finished; the draws for round 2 to the semi-finals are as a rule on the Sunday after the round, with exceptions possible, shown live by ARD or ZDF from the German Football Museum in Dortmund. Exact kick-off times are published on DFB.de about one to two weeks after the draw, agreed with the clubs, the police information office (ZIS), the DFL and the TV partners. In 2026-27 the second-round draw was on a Saturday in September 2026, during the ARD Sportschau.

text: What the winner gains and prize money. The 2026-27 Supercup was between the league runner-up Borussia Dortmund and the double winner FC Bayern. Prize money per round is not published on the pages read; the regulation says 90 % of the media and perimeter-advertising income the DFB GmbH & Co. basis: published: 2026/2027 information page; Durchführungsbestimmungen §§ 51 and 52

text: Tickets for a tie. The home club stages it, and the income from tickets and perimeter advertising is shared between the two clubs after VAT, 15 % event costs (first round 25 %) and referee and goal-line-technology costs. The away club is entitled to 10 % of the seated and 10 % of the standing tickets (at a Bundesliga club's home cup game at least 100 of them sponsor tickets, at a 2. Bundesliga club's at least 30, under a roof); with no standing places in the away section, at least 600 other tickets at reduced prices; away supporters may not be charged more than home supporters; 10 % of the places for disabled spectators go to the away club. League season tickets are valid only for league matches, not for cup ties.
basis: published: Durchführungsbestimmungen § 25 and § 50

text: Tickets for the final, as done for the 2025-26 final (nothing for 2027 published on the pages read): each finalist got a contingent and told its fans about the sale on its own channels; the tickets for the public sale were allocated by lottery among applicants after an application phase; disabled spectators applied through a separate form; VIP tickets were sold in the DFB ticket portal. Which end each finalist's fans get was drawn at the semi-finalists' meeting.
basis: observed-past-cycle: DFB news of April 2026 on the 2025-26 final

text: History. The first competition was 1934-35, then called the DFB-Vereinspokalmeisterschaft (final in December 1935 in Düsseldorf, 1. FC Nürnberg 2:0 FC Schalke 04). The DFB's list has 83 seasons up to 2025-26, none from 1943-44 to 1951-52, and the DFB called the May 2026 final the 83rd. Record winner FC Bayern München, 21 titles in 25 finals; then Werder Bremen 6 (10 finals) and FC Schalke 04, Borussia Dortmund and Eintracht Frankfurt with 5 each. Every final since 1985 has been at the Olympiastadion Berlin; the first final in Berlin was in 1937.
basis: published: winners list up to 2025/2026; the record table's Stand label (May 2024) is stale
